title: First Light
draft: Previs pass 1: surveyed in the Waystation at dawn; the zone's own Rook and Watch are framed where they stand. The tower's lamp is the keeper's lamp-iron on the sill, and goes out with a thread of smoke. Townsfolk who stop and turn are to come.

shots.note: Crane down from 12 m to 1.8 m just inside the south gate, looking north up the road: roofs, a dozen chimneys smoking straight up, the square, the well; right, on the skyline, the toll tower, and in its upper window, very small, a lamp still burning, pale in daylight (the roofs take it as the crane comes down). She walks in under the camera and on up the road. N7. Title: CHAPTER ONE / The Waystation.
Behind the west guard, his shoulder in frame: he watches her go. GD1, to the other guard, not to her, flat, a thing said every week; and watches her too long after.

Tracking behind her at her pace, over her shoulder, north: ahead of her people stop and look: the man with the ladder turns so it swings; the woman at the well holds the bucket halfway; the child runs. Nobody speaks.

Over Rook's right shoulder at the inn door, low, her head and folded arms soft in the left third: focus pulls from her to the survivor stopping at the square's edge, right of centre, looking round at the faces. Behind the survivor and above, the toll tower. Rook looks at her; then lifts her head to the tower. (Hunter: the look holds a beat longer, and her arms tighten.)

From the square by her, compressed: the tower's upper window, the keeper's lamp-iron standing on the sill, its flame pale in the shade, goes out. A thread of smoke climbs the glass. (Rook's own eyeline is blocked by the roofs; this is the nearest clear line.)
Reverse: Rook's single from the square, her eyeline just off the lens to the right. Her eyes come down from the tower to the survivor, and she unfolds her arms.
Rise and swing into the follow camera: the square, the survivor in it, Rook at her door. Bars out; Rook's mark comes up. Control. (No zone title: the chapter's card was it.)
